title: RevocationChecker and SigningKey traits bind implementors to pre-release x509-cert rc type
description: RevocationChecker::check() takes &x509_cert::Certificate and SigningKey::certificate() returns &x509_cert::Certificate, where x509_cert is pinned at `=0.3.0-rc.4` — a pre-release crate. Any caller implementing either trait must add the same pinned pre-release dependency to their Cargo.toml. This is an implementation detail (the CMS crate required this rc version) leaking through the public trait interface. What goes wrong: implementors cannot use the stable x509-cert 0.2 API alongside this crate; they are forced into the rc ecosystem until rc stabilizes. The encrypt() function also takes `recipients: &[Certificate]` directly for the same reason. One mitigation is DER-byteslice trait methods (pass &[u8] and let the crate re-parse internally); a more complete fix waits for the rc to stabilize. At minimum, document in every affected public item that the type comes from x509-cert 0.3.0-rc.4 and will change when the rc stabilizes. Affected: smime-tree/src/key.rs (RevocationChecker, SigningKey), smime-tree/src/encrypt.rs (encrypt signature).
close_reason: x509-cert RC type in trait bounds is inherent to the pre-release RustCrypto stack (same root cause as MIME-8zt.79). Cannot abstract away without losing type-level compatibility with the cms crate. Will resolve when x509-cert stabilizes.
